thread:
maria: quick sanity-check thread for the new prefetch+staged-sampling flow. sharing high-level results and how we ran it.

maria: goal = reduce p50 token latency for interactive prompts by prefetching KV for likely continuations and doing a lightweight candidate sampler, then verify/correct with the main model. keep quality regressions <1% on QA accuracy.

ajay: nice. which model/config did you test?

maria: Llama3-7b int4 (our q4f/awq build), context length 4k, batch=1 on a single A100. three modes compared:
- baseline: standard greedy/generation on quantized model
- prefetch-stage: prefetch KV for prefix+topk candidates via a cheap sampler, then verify with main loop
- async-prefetch: background KV prefetch for next 64 tokens while streaming

leo: curious about the cheap sampler. temp/beam/topk?

maria: cheap sampler = multinomial(top_k=20, temp=0.8) on a distilled 1.3B candidate model (same tokenizer). we only fetch KV for the highest-prob candidate per token. fallback to full decode if verifier confidence <0.6.

jessica: how did you measure verifier confidence?

maria: verifier is the main model scoring logits for the candidate. confidence = softmax(candidate_logit / T) where T=1.2 normalized by prefix entropy. heuristic but consistent.

maria: commands used (local harness):
```bash
python run_inference.py --model llm3-7b-int4 --mode prefetch-stage \
  --candidate_model distilled-1.3b --topk 20 --verify_thresh 0.6 \
  --eval_prompts data/eval/500_prompts.jsonl --output out/prefetch.jsonl
```

ajay: what eval set?

maria: 500 prompts sampled from our interactive suite (mix of instruction, code, QA, summarization). we track: p50/p95 token latency, per-response token cost, QA accuracy (SQuAD-like exact match), and a simple hallucination proxy (contradiction count vs. ground truth).

maria: results summary:
- baseline p50 token latency: 18ms, p95: 75ms
- prefetch-stage p50 token latency: 11ms (1.6x speedup), p95: 68ms
- async-prefetch p50: 10.5ms, p95: 80ms (spikes when mispredicted candidate)
- QA exact-match: baseline 74.3%, prefetch-stage 73.7% (-0.6pp), async-prefetch 72.9% (-1.4pp)
- regression profile: most drops are on long-context QA (>800 tokens) and multi-step code generation where candidate sampler picked a syntactically valid but semantically wrong continuation.

leo: nice perf win for median. p95 not great for async — expected. any failure modes logged?

maria: yes, created small set of 42 failure cases where verifier fallback was slow or candidate led to irreversible generation (e.g., changed function signature). attached snippets in out/failures.jsonl. common pattern: candidate picks punctuation that short-circuits a parser-based postprocessor.

jessica: did you rerun with a higher verify_thresh? tradeoffs?

maria: raise to 0.75 -> QA improves to -0.2pp vs baseline but p50 regresses to 12.8ms. diminishing returns beyond 0.8.

ajay: what about candidate model quality? distilled-1.3b might be the bottleneck.

maria: we tried distilled-3b as well (same build). candidate accuracy improved and overall QA loss reduced to -0.3pp with p50=12ms. cost increased for candidate sampling ~+8% CPU.

leo: how reproducible? seeds?

maria: each config ran 3 seeds, variance in QA <0.2pp, latency variance small. logs stored in s3://redwood-experiments/prefetch_staged/1748001234/.

infra-bot: deploy job finished for harness-v2 on infra-ml-006 (job id 4827) :white_check_mark:

maria: notes on eval methodology that we should standardize if we keep exploring:
- always include a mixed instruction/code/QA split (we saw larger regressions on code).
- use both exact-match and a soft similarity (embedding cosine) to catch "mostly correct" answers.
- flag irreversible-token patterns (e.g., function signature changes) and evaluate separately.
- sanity check with human sampling of 50 outputs for each config.

ajay: good checklist. next steps?

maria: action items: @ajay run distilled-3b candidate across the full 2k prompt eval set and push results to the same bucket. @leo can you add the irreversible-token detector to the eval harness? @jessica annotate 50 human samples for prefetch-stage. I'll prepare a short writeup for comp-perf meeting.

jessica: ack, will take the human sampling.

leo: will add detector this week. quick Q: should we try quantization change (q5_0) to see if verifier scoring shifts?

\mamaria: yes, add q5_0 run but low priority. could affect candidate scoring so treat as a separate axis.

ajay: final note — we should record model-drift artifacts: candidate sampler sometimes prefers shorter tokens; consider length-penalty in sampling.

maria: good catch. will try length-penalty 0.7 next.

maria: thanks all, saving the full thread here so folks can follow experiment steps. emoji :rocket:
